To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel method to train extractors from unlabeled data by using a relevant database and that we show that the proposed method improves extraction accuracy over a state-of-the-art method that does not utilize a database.
We propose a novel algorithm that uses a partially labeled text sequence and an incomplete relevant database to train an information extractor that fills in missing labels.
(i) a simple high-precision heuristic can label text strings that are partially similar to a database and (ii) a machine learning algorithm can be trained to fill in the remaining missing labels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can we train a supervised machine learning algorithm for information extraction from unlabeled text using relevant databases?
the problem of learning extractors from unlabeled text using relevant databases.
training extractors from unlabeled text using a labeled database.

the presented method is a useful addition to the tool box of the information extraction researcher, especially for tasks with large amounts of unlabeled data.

we show that it is possible to train an information extraction system using an unlabeled text corpus and a relevant database.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, given a large amount of text strings that are partially labeled, we show how we can use a relevant database to improve extraction accuracy.
we show that it is possible to learn extractors using unlabeled text and labeled databases.
we can learn a good extractor from an incomplete database.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of relevant databases for training extractors can significantly improve performance, especially when there are no labeled examples available.
it is possible to train extractors that are robust to missing labels and that utilize labeled fields in the database.
, in some cases, a small amount of unlabeled training data can be used to train an extractor that is more accurate than an extractor trained only on labeled data from the database.
